watchlist.reason: The free tier is published — "Start free on zero-cost models", 15+ models at 10 RPM and 100 RPD — and what it serves is other gateways' free lanes: the :free ids in its keyless catalog are ling-3.0-flash-vl:free, ling-3.0-flash-sante:free, ling-3.0-flash-fin:free, nex-n2.5-pro:free, nex-n2.5-mini:free, dots-3-note-preview:free, lfm-2.5-2.6b:free and nemotron-3.5-lightning:free, the lane OpenRouter and Kilo already carry here. The paid catalog prices frontier models well under their makers' rates — gpt-5.6-sol at $1/$5 per 1M against OpenAI's $4/$20, claude-sonnet-5 at $1/$5 — with no statement of where they are served from.
watchlist.reopen_if: NagaAI's free lane carries a model it serves itself, or it states where its below-list frontier capacity comes from.

watchlist.name: Command Code
watchlist.reason: A coding agent for open models whose cheapest plan is paid. The home page FAQ says "Free tier for solo developers", but the pricing page starts at "Go $1 /month + processing fee" with $10 of credits, then GOAT at $10/mo with $70. The free models it advertises — "Free on Laguna S 2.1 Free on Ling 3.0 Flash Free on LongCat 2.0 Free on Ling 3.0 Flash Sante", "Requests cost no credits while capacity lasts" — are listed inside those plans, not beside them.
watchlist.reopen_if: Command Code offers a $0 plan with model usage included.

watchlist.name: Kimchi (CAST AI)
watchlist.reason: CAST AI's open-source coding agent. The $0 Community tier is the harness alone — "Bring your own inference - Kimchi's managed API, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or any LLM provider. No hosted inference" — and model usage starts on Coder at $20/mo, which "Includes $25 monthly credits". The "no credit card" on the home page is about installing the CLI.
watchlist.reopen_if: The Community tier includes hosted inference or credits.

watchlist.name: EUrouter
watchlist.reason: An EU-compliance routing gateway whose Free plan prices the routing, not the tokens: "Free €0 /mo Pay for what you use Monthly limit: 10K requests/month Rate limit: 60 RPM 15% markup", and its keyless catalog prices every one of its 147 rows.
watchlist.reopen_if: A model in the eurouter.ai catalog is priced at zero, or the Free plan includes token usage.

watchlist.name: Featherless AI
watchlist.reason: Subscriptions only: "Chat For roleplay, stories and long conversations ... $25 /month" and "Developer For coding agents and API traffic ... $50 /credits per month", over a catalog of 40,000+ open models every row of which is priced. OmniRoute lists it with a free tier and then corrects itself — the only free access is an application-gated builder programme.
watchlist.reopen_if: Featherless publishes a free plan or a free model lane.

watchlist.name: StepFun (阶跃星辰)
watchlist.reason: Every model on platform.stepfun.com/docs/zh/guides/pricing/details is priced, and the page records its free lanes ending rather than starting: "Step Audio R1.1 已升级为 Step Audio R1.5。该模型已结束限时免费" (the limited-time free period is over) and "step-2x-large 已于 2026 年 06 月 12 日 结束限时免费" (ended on 2026-06-12). The home page sells the Step Plan coding subscription. Step 3.7 Flash is free through Kilo, which this list carries.
watchlist.reopen_if: StepFun's pricing page shows a zero-priced model or a signup grant.

watchlist.name: Zylo AI
watchlist.reason: The Basic plan is real — "$0 /mo 7.2k req/day · 10/min 200k Daily Tokens Basic models only ... No credits", no card — and it can only reach the rows priced at zero, since Basic carries no credits. Those rows, in the keyless catalog's BASIC tier, are nemotron-3-ultra, mistral-large-3 (675B), qwen-3.5 (397B), qwen-3.5-flash, mistral-small-4, gpt-oss-20b, step-3.7, diffusiongemma and llama-3.2-3b, plus Zylo's own routers — the models NVIDIA's API catalog serves free for development, handed out here under a gateway's free plan without a word on where they run. Terms on zyloai.net/terms cover only linked-account enforcement.
watchlist.reopen_if: Zylo states where its zero-priced Basic models are served from, or the Basic plan covers a model it serves itself.

watchlist.name: Speka
watchlist.reason: A $1 monthly allowance with no card — "Free $0.00 /mo ... $1 of model usage / month 10 requests / minute 1 API key Access to all open models" — on a gateway that markets "27 frontier models" and serves seven from its keyless catalog: nemotron-3-ultra, nemotron-3-super, gpt-oss-20b, laguna-xs-2.1, llama-3.2-11b-vision, flux.1-dev and an embedder, ids spelled the way NVIDIA's API catalog spells them. Prices sit above the makers' (DeepSeek V4 Flash at $0.27/$1.10), which is not the relay pattern, but the terms (June 2026) name no company and nothing says whose capacity the allowance spends.
watchlist.reopen_if: Speka names its operator and where its models are served, and the catalog carries what the home page claims.

watchlist.name: Logfare
watchlist.reason: "Free LLM Inference. No Limits", with the price stated plainly — "In exchange for free inference, we log every request — prompts, completions, and metadata. After PII scrubbing this may be used in our private, internal evaluation datasets" — and an operator described only as "an independent research and engineering group"; /terms and /about answer 404, and the privacy policy names no company. The keyless catalog is 19 ids, and 14 of them — glm-5.3, kimi-k2.6, qwen-3.8-27b, gemma-4-26b, melotts, aura-2-en, nova-3, lucid-origin, phoenix-1.0 and the flux and whisper builds — are Cloudflare Workers AI's names, whose free allocation is 10,000 neurons a day per account. Unlimited free use of it is either paid for by someone unnamed or pooled.
watchlist.reopen_if: Logfare publishes terms naming its operator and a stated quota, or says how the inference is paid for.

watchlist.name: OpenAdapter
watchlist.reason: OpenAdapter, Inc. sells a coding subscription — "4x Cheaper than Claude Code", Lite at $9/mo for "~400 requests over 5h" — across 72+ open models, and does have a free plan: "Try OpenAdapter Strict daily quota across the full catalog. No credit card." The quota is never given a number, and the pitch is resale on its own words: "Same models. Fraction of the price. One subscription replaces 3+ separate provider plans", beside an "0G Network" section of privately hosted models. Nothing says which provider plans are being replaced, or under what licence.
watchlist.reopen_if: OpenAdapter publishes the free plan's daily quota and where its models are served from.

watchlist.name: Free.ai
watchlist.reason: A consumer suite of 477+ tools whose free allowance is real and small in the way that matters here: "Anonymous users get 6,000 tokens/day. Sign up free for 30,000 tokens/day", spent on "Qwen 2.5 for chat" — 2024-era 7B to 72B models on its own GPUs — while "GPT-6, Claude, Veo + 584 premium models" start at $5. The API sits at api.free.ai/v1/chat/ with ids like qwen7b rather than a model a coding agent would be pointed at.
watchlist.reopen_if: The free daily allowance covers a current coding model on the API.

watchlist.name: GreenPT
watchlist.reason: EU-hosted chat on renewable energy, where the free part is a trial and the API is paid: "All API usage requires an active Pro, Teams, or API-only subscription", every plan comes "with a 14-day free trial included", and the entry plan is €4,50/month for 15 prompts a day.
watchlist.reopen_if: GreenPT's API gets a free allowance outside the subscription trial.

watchlist.name: Synthetic
watchlist.reason: A flat subscription for open models — "Subscription Packs ... $1 /day $30 /mo Rate Limit 500 requests/5hr" — with the alternative "All models are pay-per-token". No free plan or grant on the pricing page.
watchlist.reopen_if: Synthetic offers a free plan or signup allowance.

watchlist.name: NLP Cloud
watchlist.reason: OmniRoute's changelog says the free tier "is a recurring monthly free plan (10,000 requests/month)", and nothing on the vendor's side can be read to confirm it: nlpcloud.com/pricing answers a Cloudflare "Just a moment... Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue" challenge from this network and from a GitHub runner alike (2026-09-14), and api.nlpcloud.io/v1/models is a 404. The same OmniRoute file marks its terms "avoid" for proxy use.
watchlist.reopen_if: A pricing or docs page an ordinary HTTP client can read states the free plan.

watchlist.name: Baichuan (百川)
watchlist.reason: A mainland console with nothing readable: platform.baichuan-ai.com renders 108 characters, and api.baichuan-ai.com/v1/models answers api_key_empty. OmniRoute's own correction is that "current reality is only a one-time 80 CNY trial credit for new users (valid 3 months)" — a trial, and on the same mainland-registration terms that keep the other Chinese consoles off this list.
watchlist.reopen_if: A readable page states the grant and a registration open outside the mainland.

watchlist.name: gitlawb
watchlist.reason: A crypto-native agent platform — "Sponsored tips funded with USDC", spending permissions "on a Base wallet" — whose opengateway catalog prices 13 of its 14 ids and zeroes one, nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free, a model this list already carries free on five rows. OmniRoute's note is that its free MiMo access "was removed in May 2026" and the Nemotron row is "a temporary promotional model".
watchlist.reopen_if: gitlawb publishes a free lane of its own beyond one promotional id.

watchlist.name: MonsterAPI
watchlist.reason: Unreachable: monsterapi.ai and api.monsterapi.ai both answer SERVFAIL on Google's public resolver (2026-09-14), so no page or catalog can be read. The free tier OmniRoute last described was one-time trial credits with "0 credits/month" recurring.
watchlist.reopen_if: The domain resolves again and a readable page states a free allowance.

watchlist.name: Amp
watchlist.reason: Free today only with inference you bring. The Hobby tier announced on 2026-09-13 is "Free" with "Use your ChatGPT sub & other subs", "Bring your own keys (BYOK)" and "Pay-as-you-go for orbs", and the announcement says it outright: "Amp is now free to use when you bring your own compute and model subscriptions/keys ... You can still pay for model inference through Amp if you want, with no markup." The bundled lane Amp was known for is gone: its 2025-10-15 Amp Free post now opens "Update 4: Amp Free is paused. We don't intend to bring it back", after the ad-funded $10 a day of 2026-01-08 and "Amp Free Is Full (For Now)" on 2026-02-10.
watchlist.reopen_if: Amp brings back a free credit grant or a free mode that needs no subscription or key of your own.

watchlist.name: Factory (Droid)
watchlist.reason: No free plan. Individual plans start at "Pro $20 / mo", then Plus at $100 and Max at $200, and the free-sounding parts are inside them: "Droid Core: free open-weight model pool with separate Rate Limits after Standard Usage runs out" and "BYOK is free up to an allowance on all Individual plans" both describe what a subscription includes (docs.factory.ai/pricing/individuals).
watchlist.reopen_if: Factory offers a $0 plan whose Droid Core or other model usage needs no subscription.

watchlist.name: OpenHands Cloud
watchlist.reason: The free hosted tier bundles no model usage: "Individual Free — Bring your own key or use our providers at-cost", ten conversations a day, and the FAQ spells out the second half — "the OpenHands LLM provider (available within the Individual Tier), which provides multiple model options at cost, with no markup on a pay-as-you-go basis". The agent is hosted free; the inference is yours to pay for or bring, the aider case.
watchlist.reopen_if: OpenHands Cloud includes model credits or a free model on its Individual tier.

watchlist.name: Meta Model API (Muse Spark, Muse Code)
watchlist.reason: Pay-as-you-go behind a card. dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits.md prices muse-spark-1.3 at $1.25/$4.25 per 1M and its Contributor tier — the model Cline's free lane carries as cline-free/muse-spark-1.3-contributor — at $0.10/$0.20, "Heavily discounted token pricing in exchange for permission to use your prompts and completions to train future Meta models". The help center's sign-up article: "To start making requests, set up two more things: Add a payment method ... Create an API key." The docs mention "platform free-tier credits" with no figure; the only figure is in the site config shipped with every docs page for the dashboard's welcome dialog, "You have $20 in free credits to start building right away" — a one-off grant on the far side of that card. Meta's own cookbook README still says "the preview is free", the pricing page being the later word. Muse Code, the terminal agent on the same account, is billed per token or sold as monthly subscriptions. The help center renders only in a browser; the docs are readable as Markdown.
watchlist.reopen_if: An account can make requests without a payment method, or a docs page states the free-tier credit as a figure.

watchlist.name: Qwen Code (Qwen OAuth)
watchlist.reason: The sign-in that made Qwen Code a free agent is gone, in its own docs: "The Qwen OAuth free tier was discontinued on 2026-04-15. Existing cached tokens may continue working briefly, but new requests will be rejected." The /auth menu now offers Alibaba Cloud's Coding Plan ("weekly quota included", for a fixed monthly fee), a Token Plan, a Model Studio API key or a third-party key, which leaves a BYOK agent. Alibaba's free Model Studio quota is carried here as a row of its own.
watchlist.reopen_if: Qwen Code's auth menu offers a sign-in with a free quota again.

watchlist.name: Sweep (JetBrains plugin)
watchlist.reason: A one-off trial on Sweep's own models with nothing readable about its terms. sweep.dev/pricing offers "Free Trial Free Try Sweep risk-free 1,000 Autocompletes $5 API credits included", then Basic at $10 a month for unlimited autocomplete, Pro at $20 and Ultra at $60. The documentation it links answers HTTP 402 (docs.sweep.dev, 2026-09-14) and its terms and blog URLs serve the home page, so neither the trial's conditions nor whether it takes a card can be read.
watchlist.reopen_if: Sweep publishes the trial's terms on a page that answers, card or no card, or adds a recurring free allowance.

watchlist.name: 01.AI (Yi API)
watchlist.reason: 01.AI closed its model API: api.lingyiwanwu.com answers GET /v1/models with HTTP 410 {"error":{"code":"model_service_closed","message":"Model service has been discontinued"}}. The company is alive on the same domain — www.lingyiwanwu.com announces "2026.07 万策平台发布", an enterprise decision platform — so the offer ended, not the service. It sat on the blocklist from 2026-09-14 as a product that was gone, which would have buried a vendor that can reopen an API. OmniRoute's feed still names its "Yi-Light" free models.
watchlist.reopen_if: api.lingyiwanwu.com/v1/models serves models again, or 01.AI publishes API pricing with a free allowance.

watchlist.name: Cerebras Inference
watchlist.reason: Listed from 2026-07-19 to 2026-09-16 as a trial marked with a card, and taken off because CONTRIBUTING excludes one-off credits that require one. inference-docs.cerebras.ai/support/rate-limits: "New accounts receive $5 in free credits after adding a verified payment method. These credits expire 30 days after they’re granted", "If you skip adding a payment method at sign-up, Playground and API access remain inactive until you do", and "Is there a permanently free tier? No."
watchlist.reopen_if: Cerebras grants credits without a payment method, or a free allowance that recurs.

watchlist.name: Infomaniak AI Services
watchlist.reason: Listed from 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-16 as a trial marked with a card, and taken off because CONTRIBUTING excludes one-off credits that require one: "One million free credits allow you to test the service without commitment for one month" and "A credit card is required to start using the API" (support guide 2845).
watchlist.reopen_if: The trial credits stop requiring a card, or a free allowance recurs.

watchlist.name: Scaleway Generative APIs
watchlist.reason: Listed from 2026-07-20 to 2026-09-16 as a free tier marked with a card, and taken off because CONTRIBUTING excludes one-off credits that require one. "Every new customer gets 1,000,000 free tokens—start paying only from the 1,000,001st token" is a once-per-customer grant, and Scaleway's account docs say "Ordering Scaleway resources requires a valid credit card".
watchlist.reopen_if: The free tokens stop requiring a card, or become a recurring allowance.

watchlist.name: Aiberm
watchlist.reason: A paid relay with nothing free found and no cause shown. It sat on the blocklist from 2026-09-14 on its own discount claim ("85–90% off Claude, 90% off GPT"), and a price is not provenance. Its FAQ separates "claude-" models, discounted and "best suited for coding scenarios", from "anthropic/" models "Routed through AWS", without saying where the first kind come from. aiberm.org is its mainland mirror.
watchlist.reopen_if: Aiberm offers a free allowance, or states where its discounted Claude capacity comes from.

watchlist.name: AKI.IO
watchlist.reason: A European inference API hosted in Germany whose free user account gets trial credit with no card — "Business and professional users can create a free user account and receive trial credit for API evaluation. Depending on the models used, this covers millions of tokens. No credit card is required, and the trial does not automatically convert into a paid service." — but no page gives the credit a figure or the trial a length. The terms say only that "The trial period ends as specified on the website when applying for the trial period", and that the service "is reserved for entrepreneurs" acting in a trade, business or profession, with a company account (register number and VAT ID) needed once the trial ends. A credit with no figure gives a probe nothing that ends with it, the Baseten case.
watchlist.reopen_if: AKI.IO publishes the size or the length of the trial credit on a readable page.

watchlist.name: RunInfra
watchlist.reason: Hosted model APIs on a prepaid balance, with a one-off dollar: the docs say "Signing up is free and grants $1 once per account" and the pricing page "New accounts start with $1 free to test the Model APIs", top-ups starting at $10 after that. A one-off credit is listed here when it asks for no card, and neither page, nor the pricing FAQ, says whether this one can be spent before a payment method is added (2026-09-17).
watchlist.reopen_if: A RunInfra page says the $1 is spent without a payment method on file.

watchlist.name: Kosmik Compute
watchlist.reason: A Prague-hosted API whose one chat model is Qwen3.8 27B, beside Whisper and text-to-speech models, offering "€10 in free credits when you sign up to try our API for free". Nothing on the home page or on any page its docs index lists says whether a card is needed before the credit is spent — the question that decides a one-off credit here, as it does on SiliconFlow.
watchlist.reopen_if: A Kosmik page says the €10 is spent without a payment method on file.

watchlist.name: Modelis
watchlist.reason: An OpenAI-compatible gateway whose free tier is a RapidAPI listing: modelishub.com/pricing says "Subscribe on RapidAPI (free tier, no card to start)", and the listing's BASIC plan is $0 with a hard limit of 100 requests a month. The same listing says tools and function calling are not supported on current plans and "Output is capped at 1024 tokens" — a lane that cannot call a tool cannot drive a coding agent, the AI Horde case.
watchlist.reopen_if: The free plan accepts tool definitions and allows more than 100 requests a month.

watchlist.name: TrustedRouter
watchlist.reason: The keyless catalog prices trustedrouter/free, a routing pool, at 0 — beside orchestration aliases that also read 0 — but the pricing page bills every route: "Pay the provider price plus 5.5%, with no monthly plan", and "Prepaid text and embedding prices are provider cost + 5.5%, with a $0.01 per million token floor", paid from prepaid credits, BYOK or usage-based billing. Its only credits are migration credits for "Teams already spending more than $100/month on LLMs", by approval.
watchlist.reopen_if: TrustedRouter exempts trustedrouter/free from the floor or publishes a free allowance.

watchlist.name: Umans AI (Umans Code)
watchlist.reason: Open coding models on the vendor's own GPUs, paid from a wallet: "A wallet with no credit at all — no paid top-up, no active promo grant — does not serve until it has some", the first rate tier unlocks at "Your first top-up", and promo credit such as the founders' bonus serves only while it lasts. The keyless catalog prices one id at 0, umans-deepseek-v4.1-flash-lab, which the docs never name; the one lab they describe, DeepSeek V4 Pro, "served here as a seat-gated pre-release lab". models.dev also lists an Umans AI Coding Plan at cost 0, and the docs speak of plans only as archived plans.
watchlist.reopen_if: Umans serves an account with no top-up, or documents a zero-priced model any account can call.

watchlist.name: IO Intelligence (io.net)
watchlist.reason: The plans page gives the default Standard plan "free, light daily access", with pay-as-you-go beyond "the daily limit", and the table on the same page describes Standard as "Continuous access with PAYG" with "No refreshes, pay only for what you use". No figure for the free access appears on any page read. The keyless catalog prices all 35 rows and opens four to the lowest access tier — GLM-4.5-Air, Gemma 4 26B A4B, gpt-oss-20b and Llama 3.3 70B — the rest needing a higher one.
watchlist.reopen_if: io.net publishes the Standard plan's daily free allowance with a figure.

watchlist.name: Qiniu AI inference (七牛云)
watchlist.reason: New AI-inference users get a one-time package — 注册有奖活动：现在注册 qiniu.com/ai 开发者账号，立即获得 300万免费 Token 资源包, three million tokens counted at DeepSeek-V3.1's input price — issued after the first billed usage (使用服务并产生计费后自动发放). Two walls keep it off. The API FAQ says 目前AI产品仅支持中国大陆账号使用，暂不支持海外账号 — the AI products take mainland-China accounts only, not overseas ones — and a new user has a 24-hour grace period (24 小时免认证体验期) before real-name verification is required: the mainland real-name account this list does not carry, as for Baidu Qianfan and Volcengine.
watchlist.reopen_if: Qiniu opens AI inference to accounts outside mainland China without real-name verification.

watchlist.name: IteraCompute
watchlist.reason: Nine chat models priced per token in a keyless catalog that marks every row `is_free: false`; neither the home page nor the docs page names a free allowance, a trial or a signup credit (2026-09-17).
watchlist.reopen_if: A row marked free in the catalog, or a signup credit with a figure on a vendor page.

watchlist.name: Eden AI
watchlist.reason: A unified API whose keyless catalog prices 1,064 rows, a handful at 0 — google/gemma-4-31b-it, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it and cohere/command-a-plus-05-2026 among them — while billing is a credit system: "Eden AI uses a pay-per-use credit system", credits are bought with a 5.5% platform fee, and the pricing page names no signup credit. Whether a zero-priced row answers an account with no credit is stated on no page read, the question NanoGPT's record turns on.
watchlist.reopen_if: Eden AI's docs say zero-priced models run on an empty balance, or a signup credit is named.

watchlist.name: Vultr Serverless Inference
watchlist.reason: A paid subscription: the docs provision "a Vultr Serverless Inference subscription" before a key exists, and neither they nor the API reference at api.vultrinference.com name a free allowance. vultr.com's pricing pages answer 403 to a script (2026-09-17); the keyless catalog lists 16 models.
watchlist.reopen_if: Vultr publishes a free inference allowance that needs no subscription.

watchlist.name: Wallaby
watchlist.reason: Kimi K3 on a prepaid balance — "Top up — prepaid USD, from $20" — from Wallaby Data Pty Ltd in Australia. The terms mention a trial no page quantifies: "new accounts may receive promotional trial credit", which "may be restricted to specific models and lower rate limits".
watchlist.reopen_if: Wallaby publishes a trial credit with a figure.

watchlist.name: Vivgrid
watchlist.reason: The Free plan is a platform tier rather than an allowance — "$0 to start Pay-as-you-go model usage" — and the credits on offer are the Growth plan's "$25 in token credits included every month", at $25 a month, and "$200/mo credits available to approved open-source maintainers on request", a grant by approval rather than a tier anyone can use. The operator is Allegro US, LLC.
watchlist.reopen_if: The Free plan includes model usage with a figure.

watchlist.name: NaN (nan.builders)
watchlist.reason: A paid membership, not a free tier: "A closed community of builders sharing dedicated GPUs to run open models. Every member pays to be here", paid by "Credit or debit card", with a waitlist for spots. models.dev lists its seven models at cost 0 because the price is the flat subscription; the monthly token allowances per member are what it buys.
watchlist.reopen_if: NaN offers a membership or an allowance at no charge.

watchlist.name: EBCloud (英博云)
watchlist.reason: The model API spends purchased compute points — 在正式使用模型API服务前，需先购买算力点。算力点购买仅支持通过英博云账户现金余额进行支付 — bought before the first call and only from cash balance, on an account that has done 注册和实名认证, registration and real-name verification. The ¥20 the home page gives for registering and verifying (注册认证送20元无门槛代金券) is a voucher, where the points are bought with cash balance only.
watchlist.reopen_if: The model API accepts vouchers or offers a free allowance, without real-name verification.

watchlist.name: Berget.AI
watchlist.reason: A Swedish inference API whose Trial plan has "€5 free starting credits", but the pricing FAQ puts a card in front of them: "The Trial plan includes €5 in starting credits so you can try the API without a subscription — a card is required at signup to prevent abuse, but nothing is charged." After the credit, "an active plan (from €25 / month in prepaid credits) is required for continued API access". One-off credits behind a card are what CONTRIBUTING excludes.
watchlist.reopen_if: The €5 is granted without a card, or a free allowance recurs without a plan.

watchlist.name: CloudFerro Sherlock
watchlist.reason: Sherlock, CloudFerro's model API, is billed per token — "Our pricing model is based on token usage - both input (received) and output (generated) tokens for each model" — and "To use Sherlock’s API, you have to be an admin user of an Organization registered at CloudFerro", an organization that needs an EU VAT number or tax ID. The cloud's free trial ("We grant up to 250 EUR for testing purposes within our infrastructure") is not said on any page read to reach Sherlock tokens.
watchlist.reopen_if: A CloudFerro page says the trial credits pay for Sherlock, without a card or a company tax ID.

watchlist.name: Crusoe
watchlist.reason: The pricing page offers "$5 in free credits" to "Fine-tune and serve models in Crusoe Intelligence Foundry", while managed inference is pay-as-you-go per million tokens, and the account docs put a card in front of both: "To provision resources or use the managed inference service, you must enable billing on your account. You will need a valid, non-prepaid credit card to proceed."
watchlist.reopen_if: The $5 can be spent on inference before a card is added.

watchlist.name: DigitalOcean Serverless Inference
watchlist.reason: A new team gets a signup credit — "When you create your first team, DigitalOcean automatically applies a $5 signup credit" and "Signup credits expire 90 days after signup" — but a payment method comes first ("You must add a valid payment method before you can create Droplets or other resources"), and "Serverless inference is prepaid only. You must maintain a positive prepaid account balance to send serverless inference requests". Whether the signup credit counts toward that balance is not stated.
watchlist.reopen_if: DigitalOcean documents the signup credit paying for serverless inference with no payment method on file.

watchlist.name: evroc Think
watchlist.reason: evroc's shared models are billed per token, and two posts from September 2026 offer a campaign: "For the first 100 signups, we are offering €300 credits to help you get a started building on evroc and using evroc Think." The sign-up form's own script saves a card before the account exists — "Save Payment Method (€0 charge)" — and the billing docs say "At least one card must remain on your account". A first-100 grant behind a card is excluded twice over.
watchlist.reopen_if: evroc offers credits that are claimed without saving a card.

watchlist.name: GMI Cloud (Inference Engine)
watchlist.reason: Serverless models are paid from bought credit, their prices kept in the console ("Rather than mirror prices here (where they would go stale), the up-to-date rates live in the console"), and usage tiers follow purchases — "Please note that voucher redemptions do not count towards purchase". No page read names a signup credit or a zero-priced model; the GMI Router's free model selection routes to paid models.
watchlist.reopen_if: GMI publishes a signup credit or a zero-priced serverless model.

watchlist.name: Inceptron
watchlist.reason: "Only pay for what you run. Simple, transparent, and built for real usage. No hidden fees." — six serverless models, every one priced in the keyless catalog, plus dedicated GPUs from $3 an hour with commitment discounts; no free tier, trial credit or zero price on any page read.
watchlist.reopen_if: A signup credit or a zero-priced model on an Inceptron page or catalog.

watchlist.name: Inco
watchlist.reason: A prepaid, per-token API behind a waitlist: "Access is prepaid. Credit is consumed per token at the rates shown at the time of each request. Requests are rejected when your balance reaches zero." The terms also say "Inco is an experimental prototype." No starting credit is named.
watchlist.reopen_if: Inco grants starting credit at sign-up.

watchlist.name: Jalapeno Cloud
watchlist.reason: The offer exists only in the site's JavaScript, and the same scripts disagree with it. The pricing page's script says "Flexible token pricing, high usage limits, and postpaid billing—plus $1 in free credits to get you started!", a partner campaign's says "Sign in to get $1 in free credits instantly.", and the home page's quick start says "Top up your account with credits to enable API calls." Every one of the 20 models in the keyless catalog is priced. The operator named in the recharge agreement is Magik Compute Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.
watchlist.reopen_if: A server-rendered Jalapeno page states the $1 grant and that it is spent without a top-up.

watchlist.name: Klok AI-API (klokintegration.se)
watchlist.reason: A Swedish integration company's model API, currently DeepSeek V4 Flash behind the name Kloker: "Usage is billed per million tokens, excl. VAT. Input is €0.20. Output is €1.", with keys by request — "Not on the platform yet? Email klokintegration@integrera.com and ask for a token." The 30-day free trial on the home page belongs to its chat assistant, not the API.
watchlist.reopen_if: Klok grants a free token allowance for the AI-API.

watchlist.name: Lilac
watchlist.reason: Four open models on idle enterprise GPUs, per token from prepaid credits: "You need a positive credit balance before you can make API requests." The personal subscriptions ($10, $30 and $100 a month) include usage worth $20, $75 and $300, all paid; no starting credit is named.
watchlist.reopen_if: Lilac grants starting credit without a top-up.

watchlist.name: LucidQuery
watchlist.reason: A French lab's own models, AGI 01 Swift and Frontier, on a metered API — "Metered usage, no monthly minimum. Pay only for the tokens your app sends and receives." Its $0 Free plan, "A restrained entry into AGI 01, LucidArc, and LucidCode", covers the vendor's own chat, desktop and CLI apps with unpublished limits (the CLI offers "Connect with /login: free, subscription, or API key."), and nothing ties that plan to the API.
watchlist.reopen_if: LucidQuery says the Free plan's allowance works through api.lucidquery.com with a key other clients can use.

watchlist.name: Melious
watchlist.reason: "Access 60+ open-weight models on a pay-as-you-go basis. No commitments, no minimums. Just top up credits and go." The free Explorer plan in the pricing page's data carries a daily energy allowance for the vendor's studio but not API usage, and for plans like it the docs say "API calls are `credits_only`, even if you have energy left". The coding plans that do include API usage are paid and "intended exclusively for businesses as defined by § 14 BGB".
watchlist.reopen_if: Melious lets the Explorer plan or a signup grant pay for API calls.

watchlist.name: Model Oracle AI
watchlist.reason: A gateway for coding agents billed from a balance: "Prepaid usage with no subscription. Add prepaid usage balance with a card." Managed requests deduct the catalog provider cost and BYOK requests a 5% fee; no free allowance is named.
watchlist.reopen_if: Model Oracle grants balance at sign-up without a card.

watchlist.name: NeoSmith
watchlist.reason: A router that distills small models from an agent's own traces, not an open lane: "NeoSmith is currently free for design partners during early access", and the self-serve route is a booked demo that ends with a pilot key — "Walk away with a 14-day pilot key (no credit card)". A key issued after a sales call is not an offer a reader can take.
watchlist.reopen_if: NeoSmith issues keys with a free allowance through self-serve sign-up.

watchlist.name: Neuralwatt
watchlist.reason: Energy-priced inference whose trial asks for a card first: the quick start says "adding a payment method unlocks $1.00 in free trial credit (no charge required; the credit is valid for 30 days)", and the pricing page "Add a payment method to get $1.00 in free credits — no charge required — then add more when you need them."
watchlist.reopen_if: The trial credit is granted without adding a payment method.

watchlist.name: OpenReason
watchlist.reason: Company AI sold per person to businesses, with a price still unset — "We are not going to invent one to fill this page" — and no plan for one developer: "There is no single-seat plan and there will not be one." Its "Free to try" has no published terms.
watchlist.reopen_if: Published trial terms that give an individual developer an API key with a free allowance.

watchlist.name: routing.run
watchlist.reason: A membership router: "Basic is $10/month and includes $10 in routing credit. Add more whenever you need it.", and the API quick start requires "An active Basic membership with a positive Routing balance". Every row in the keyless catalog is priced.
watchlist.reopen_if: A free tier or signup credit usable without the Basic membership.

watchlist.name: 302.AI
watchlist.reason: A pay-as-you-go aggregator — 302.AI采用0月费和按用量付费模式，先充值，后扣费 (no monthly fee, pay by usage: top up first, then it is deducted) — and "The minimum recharge is $5 to use all AI products." A $1 test credit exists on paper with changing conditions: a help FAQ last modified 2024-11-07 gives it to every user who binds a phone, and a changelog entry of 2025-03-03 narrows it to 新用户只有填写邀请码才可以获得1美金测试额度 — only new users who enter an invite code; the referral-code page that entry links to answers 404.
watchlist.reopen_if: A current 302.AI page grants new accounts API credit without an invite code or a top-up.

watchlist.name: Abacus.AI RouteLLM API
watchlist.reason: The RouteLLM API comes with a subscription: "Sign up as a ChatLLM subscriber to access RouteLLM API", and "A ChatLLM subscription is $10 per user per month. You will be billed $10 when you sign up." No free API access is named.
watchlist.reopen_if: A RouteLLM API key is available to an unsubscribed account.

watchlist.name: above.dev
watchlist.reason: A router sold in prepaid packs, with no account before payment: "Buy a credit pack at https://above.dev/pricing ($10, $20 or $50). Checkout creates your account, emails your API key, and opens the dashboard for usage and balance history."
watchlist.reopen_if: An account or key obtainable before checkout, with a stated free credit.

watchlist.name: ai&
watchlist.reason: Open models hosted in Japan on prepaid credit: "ai& uses a prepaid credit model. You add credits to your organization, and inference requests deduct from that balance as they complete." Redemption codes add credit without a card, but "Redemption codes are handed out at events, hackathons and workshops". A cookbook page calls qwen/qwen3.6-27b "free for prototyping", while the keyless catalog prices it at $0.32 in and $3.20 out per million tokens (2026-09-17).
watchlist.reopen_if: A zero-priced model in the keyless catalog, or a public signup credit.

watchlist.name: Aixy
watchlist.reason: A governance gateway over the customer's own provider credentials — "Connect a provider, create a project API key, and call the gateway." — selling paid plans of its own, billed apart from inference: "This page describes inference cost attribution, not the price of an Aixy subscription." It hosts no capacity to give away. The site answers 403 to scripts; its llms-full.txt is readable.
watchlist.reopen_if: Aixy-hosted model capacity with a free allowance that needs no provider key of your own.

watchlist.name: Ambient
watchlist.reason: A verified-inference network whose API needs paid credit: "The Anthropic-compatible endpoint requires paid credits, like the OpenAI-compatible one: on the free tier requests return `402`." Its cheapest plan is $1 a month — "A small paid tier for trying Ambient." — and the keyless catalog prices all four models.
watchlist.reopen_if: Ambient's free tier or its drops can make API calls that do not return 402.

watchlist.name: Auriko
watchlist.reason: A router whose Free plan and "14-day free trial. No credit card required." are platform tiers, with inference bought separately: "Pro is a flat $89/mo subscription billed separately from inference costs. You purchase credits at provider token prices with zero markup. Credits work the same on Free and Pro." The keyless directory at api.auriko.ai/v1/directory/models prices five routes at 0, three to Z.ai and two to Google AI Studio, and no page says whether they answer an account with no credit.
watchlist.reopen_if: Auriko documents its zero-priced routes answering an account with no purchased credit.

watchlist.name: Ant Ling (Ant Group)
watchlist.reason: A real daily quota behind an Alipay payment agreement. The pricing page: "Each account receives 500,000 free tokens per day (shared across input and output). The quota resets daily at 2:00 AM UTC+8 and does not roll over.", on Ling-3.0-flash, Ling-2.6-1T, Ling-2.6-flash and Ring-2.6-1T at 2 QPS. But "Before your first API call, bind an Alipay account and activate the Ling service", the FAQ adds "You need to sign the Mini Program Cloud auto-debit agreement and activate the Ling model service", and "Only personal Alipay accounts are supported for payment." An auto-debit agreement is a payment method on file, and whether an Alipay account opened outside mainland China can sign it is stated on no page read. Ling 3.0 Flash variants are already free on rows this list carries. models.dev still lists the service as Bailing at api.tbox.cn.
watchlist.reopen_if: The daily quota works without the auto-debit agreement, or a page says an Alipay account from outside mainland China can sign it.

watchlist.name: Claudinio
watchlist.reason: Flat-rate subscriptions for coding agents. The account docs say "The first time you sign in, your account is created automatically on the Free plan, so you can try it before paying anything", but no page gives the Free plan an allowance, and the API reference lists `402` "No active subscription". The site's source carries promotional strings for a signup credit and daily free credits that no rendered page shows.
watchlist.reopen_if: A page states the Free plan's API allowance, or a signup or daily credit usable without a subscription.

watchlist.name: CoralBricks
watchlist.reason: Gated by request: "Coral Inference is currently a design-partner program. To get access, contact hello@coralbricks.ai.", and ungranted accounts get `403 access_denied`. Usage is billed from a prepaid balance.
watchlist.reopen_if: Open self-serve access with a stated free credit or free model.

watchlist.name: CrossModel
watchlist.reason: "Usage-based pricing, one unified bill, no subscriptions.", funded by Stripe top-ups with a 5.5% service fee — "There is no minimum fee — but the minimum top-up is $10." No signup credit or zero-priced model is named.
watchlist.reopen_if: A signup credit or a zero-priced model on CrossModel's own pages.

watchlist.name: DInference
watchlist.reason: Open models hosted in Tokyo at per-token prices, with direct keys handed out on request and aimed at high-volume users; the site renders only in a browser, and no page names a free tier or credit (2026-09-17).
watchlist.reopen_if: A self-serve key with a stated free allowance.

watchlist.name: d.run (DaoCloud)
watchlist.reason: A mainland platform whose token API is pay-as-you-go — MaaS by Token：使用 Token 计费，共享资源 — on an account that must pass real-name verification: 根据适用法律要求，您需要进行实名认证以使用我们的产品或服务。 The docs home still shows an undated "DeepSeek free for two weeks" banner with no terms behind it.
watchlist.reopen_if: A dated, current page grants free token usage or a signup voucher without mainland real-name verification.

watchlist.name: FrogBot
watchlist.reason: API usage draws on a paid balance — "Your subscription payments and added funds become a USD balance." — and in the plan table API access belongs to the $25 Pro plan; the Free plan's 300 credits a month cover the vendor's own agents and flows.
watchlist.reopen_if: Free-plan credits can be spent through an API key.

watchlist.name: Infer by Flow7
watchlist.reason: "Infer by Flow7 provides public paid access. Anyone can create an account; email verification and wallet funding are required before metered API use." Accounts start at $0, every selector in the keyless catalog is priced, and "Serving suppliers remain private."
watchlist.reopen_if: A free wallet credit, or a zero-priced selector in the public catalog.

watchlist.name: QuanHex (QiHang)
watchlist.reason: A reseller gateway paid by Alipay top-ups from ¥10, with email verification; the only zero-priced entry in its pricing data is an internal test model (启航测试模型，不计费，仅用于测试 — a test model, not billed, for testing only). No registration bonus is named.
watchlist.reopen_if: A registration bonus, or a zero-priced production model.

watchlist.name: Vancine
watchlist.reason: Free credit for new accounts ended on 2026-09-02: "Effective immediately, newly registered users will no longer automatically receive complimentary API credits." Since then the only credit is a one-time bonus after a first top-up of at least $5, and no model is priced at 0.
watchlist.reopen_if: The revised trial the 2026-09-02 announcement promises grants credit without a top-up.

watchlist.name: SaladCloud AI Gateway
watchlist.reason: A gateway in early access, paid per token from a credit balance or by a monthly subscription arranged with support: "The organization must have a positive credit balance before it can process AI Gateway requests." The pricing FAQ answers its own question about a free trial: "No. SaladCloud and the Transcription API are pay-as-you-go with no minimum commitment".
watchlist.reopen_if: Salad grants new organizations credit, without a card, that the AI Gateway accepts.

watchlist.name: Sakana AI (Fugu)
watchlist.reason: Paid subscriptions from $20 a month or pay-as-you-go credits — the terms read "To use the Service, You must purchase credits that may be used within the Service" — and "we do not provide services to users in EU (European Union) or EEA (European Economic Area) member states". The console's pricing page ships interface strings for a free usage allowance that no public page describes.
watchlist.reopen_if: A public Sakana page states a free API allowance for accounts without a subscription.

watchlist.name: SCNet (超算互联网)
watchlist.reason: China's national supercomputing marketplace runs a promotion from 2026-08-13 to 2026-10-13 whose new-user package is 1000万 token 量包 — ten million tokens of GLM-5-Base, valid 30 days — under 仅限活动期间新注册用户，每个账号限领1次。福利总量有限，先到先得 (new accounts only, once each, while supplies last). A base model is not what a coding agent runs, new accounts are told apart by phone number, ID-card number and payment account, and the API docs say API access may have to be opened through a business advisor (如有需要，可联系您的专属业务顾问或平台客服开通调用 API 权限). The Token Plan itself is a paid subscription for AI tools only.
watchlist.reopen_if: A recurring or chat-model allowance that opens without mainland real-name verification.

watchlist.name: KUAE Cloud Coding Plan (Moore Threads)
watchlist.reason: A GLM-4.7 coding plan with a 30-day free trial described as a promotion — 用户在推广活动期间可申请30天免费试用 — at about 40 prompts per five hours, and 套餐仅限于指定的编程工具中使用 (usable only in the listed coding tools). The claim page is client-rendered and answers "please log in first" to a script, and the launch page's own bundle limits the trial to 100 developers a day, so whether it can be claimed today, and with what account, cannot be read.
watchlist.reopen_if: A readable page shows the trial open now, with a sign-up a reader outside mainland China can complete.

watchlist.name: SCX.ai
watchlist.reason: An Australian sovereign inference provider priced per token, with monthly plans in compute units from A$500; the site answers 403 to scripts and its rendered pricing and plan pages name no free tier, trial or credit (2026-09-17).
watchlist.reopen_if: A sign-up credit or trial for new accounts on an SCX page.

watchlist.name: STACKIT AI Model Serving
watchlist.reason: A free 30-day test by application, for companies: "All registrations are manually checked by us. If you qualify, you will receive your personal token to use STACKIT AI Model Serving within 24 hours. The trial period ends automatically after 30 days." The request form requires a company name, and a customer account needs to "Provide the company’s VAT ID and Commercial Register number."
watchlist.reopen_if: Self-serve sign-up, without approval or a company, that grants a free token or credit.

watchlist.name: Subconscious
watchlist.reason: "Usage based pricing or monthly plans to power your agents efficiently." — per-token credits from the dashboard or plans from $100 a month; no free plan or trial is named.
watchlist.reopen_if: Free starting credits or a free plan on the pricing page or in the docs.

watchlist.name: Submodel (InstaGen)
watchlist.reason: Per-token open models from a funded balance, and the FAQ rules out a trial in so many words: "We don't currently offer refunds or trial credits due to the overhead of processing these requests."
watchlist.reopen_if: Trial credits or zero-priced models in the InstaGen docs.

watchlist.name: TensorX
watchlist.reason: EU inference on prepaid credits bought by card, with no free tier: "When your balance falls below $0.05, your account and API keys will be disabled."
watchlist.reopen_if: A starting credit without payment, or a zero-priced model.

watchlist.name: Tinker (Thinking Machines)
watchlist.reason: A fine-tuning API with sampling endpoints, billed by use — "Tinker uses a pricing plan that reflects usage. All prices are in USD per million tokens." — whose serverless inference is a beta for Thinking Machines' own Inkling models; research grants are the only credit mentioned.
watchlist.reopen_if: Free credits for new accounts without an application.

watchlist.name: Tinfoil
watchlist.reason: Confidential inference whose API key comes after checkout: "Complete the checkout by entering your payment details. You're only charged based on usage." Every model in the keyless catalog is priced.
watchlist.reopen_if: A starting credit without payment details, or a zero-priced model.

watchlist.name: TokenGo
watchlist.reason: "TokenGO uses a pay-as-you-go model. You only pay for the tokens you actually consume, priced per million tokens.", funded through Stripe before the first request; the "Free" row in its rate-limit table is a speed tier, not a balance.
watchlist.reopen_if: A free balance at sign-up, or a public code that grants credit without payment.

watchlist.name: Vispark Lab
watchlist.reason: Three vision models paid in units bought in rupees — the app's own text is "Buy units to continue — you'll return here after payment." — and priced in the keyless catalog; no free units are named.
watchlist.reopen_if: Free units at sign-up, or a zero-priced model.

watchlist.name: Wafer
watchlist.reason: "Access Wafer models through an OpenAI-compatible API. Add credits, create an API key, and pay per token.", or a paid Wafer Pass subscription. Its $500 of free credits belong to a startup program that begins with "a 25-minute conversation with our team".
watchlist.reopen_if: Credits for any new account without an application, or a free Wafer Pass tier.

watchlist.name: Xpersona
watchlist.reason: Paid entry only: "Choose monthly capacity from $20—or try the API with $2 prepaid credits." Every priced model in the catalog is paid.
watchlist.reopen_if: Credits granted without payment.

watchlist.name: Zenifra
watchlist.reason: A Brazilian platform whose sign-up credit reaches its AI API with no card — "Ao criar sua conta, você ganha R$30,00 em créditos automaticamente" and "Você não precisa ter cartão de crédito para começar" (a new account gets R$30 of credit automatically; no credit card is needed to start), usable on AI ("Os R$30,00 recebidos ao criar a conta também podem ser usados com a oferta de IA") — but registration asks for a "CPF ou CNPJ válido" and "residência no Brasil", a Brazilian tax ID and residence: a national identity wall, like the mainland real-name accounts recorded above.
watchlist.reopen_if: Zenifra opens registration without a Brazilian tax ID and residence.

watchlist.name: Echo by Tracer
watchlist.reason: A workspace API for agent runs rather than a chat endpoint — "The workspace API has a saved-run contract; OpenAI Chat Completions SDK request fields do not apply." — paid from workspace credit or with your own provider key: "No Tracer fee on the first $30,000/month in eligible usage per workspace with your own API key." One model in its public library, the anonymous Union Alpha preview, is flagged free, with its availability unstated.
watchlist.reopen_if: A free credit for new workspaces, or a free model callable through the API without payment.

watchlist.name: Helicone AI Gateway
watchlist.reason: The free Hobby plan's "10,000 free requests" are observability logs, not inference; the gateway serves models from bought credits or your own provider keys, and a call with neither fails — the error guide's case is "No Helicone credits, no BYOK".
watchlist.reopen_if: Free inference credit for new accounts.

watchlist.name: NEAR AI Cloud
watchlist.reason: Confidential inference on purchased credits ("purchase credits based on your needs"), every model in the keyless catalog priced. The one way in without a card is a stake: "Stake NEAR to fund private inference and deploy always-on IronClaw agents. Credits scale with your stake. No credit card required." — credits paid by the staking rewards on tokens the reader must own.
watchlist.reopen_if: Starting credits for new accounts without a purchase or a stake.

watchlist.name: CloudCode.ONE
watchlist.reason: A pay-as-you-go coding gateway (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4 Pro) whose home page FAQ says "Top up credit from $2" and names no free tier. The only statement of one is a July blog post, "CloudCode.ONE now has a free tier", published with its figures never filled in — "[X tokens / $Y worth of credit] per [day/month]" and "[The quota resets every day/month.]" — so the offer has no quota a reader could plan against. OmniRoute's config calls two GLM Flash ids there "published free model aliases".
watchlist.reopen_if: A CloudCode.ONE page states what the free tier gives, in numbers.

watchlist.name: DGrid AI Gateway
watchlist.reason: The free lane is one router id, dgridai/free, which "aggregates multiple sources of free inference capacity behind a single routing layer"; the model behind it "can change from request to request" and no page names it or its sources. 10 requests a minute and 100 a day per account, 20 and 1,000 after $5 of top-ups. Free capacity gathered from other sources is the NaraRouter verdict above: a gateway re-serving free lanes it does not own is not the vendor of the offer.
watchlist.reopen_if: DGrid names the models and the sources behind dgridai/free, and they are its own capacity or sold to it for this.

watchlist.name: HCNSec public-welfare gateway (幻城公益API)
watchlist.reason: A New API relay run by 新疆幻城网安科技有限责任公司 — its own FAQ opens with "中转站如何使用？" (how do I use the relay station?) — whose free-user group serves other vendors' models from sources it does not name. On 2026-09-06 the operator warned that the free group's glm-5.3 "是第三方低价服务商非官方服务商 模型真实度有待考证": it comes from a third-party low-price, unofficial provider, and whether it is the real model is unverified. A sign-up balance and invite rewards spent on that is not a vendor's own offer.
watchlist.reopen_if: The free group serves the operator's own deployment of a named model, with its quota on a page.

watchlist.name: LiteRouter
watchlist.reason: A subscription gateway run by Eqlyx, LLC whose $0 Basic plan gives "∞ requests/day for most of free models" — "a rate limit of up to 100 requests per hour applies to free models", its FAQ adds — and 50 premium requests a day. The free models are about forty ':free' variants of other vendors' models (DeepSeek, GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi, MiniMax, Mistral Large 3, Gemma 4, gpt-oss) and no page says where they are served from: the xKiro case above, unlisted until that is known.
watchlist.reopen_if: LiteRouter names the providers behind its :free ids, and they sell or give it that capacity.

watchlist.name: Helyx AI
watchlist.reason: A crypto-funded gateway whose pages disagree about the free offer. The home page grants "$10 free credit on signup" — "$2.000000 instant, another $8.000000 released on request" by support — and greets a visitor with "Your 0 daily claim is waiting", while the about page promises "1M free Claude Opus 5 tokens claimed daily" and the terms "the 1M daily Claude Opus 5 claim". No page names the operator: the contacts are a WhatsApp number and a Telegram handle, and the privacy page says only that "we route requests to upstream providers".
watchlist.reopen_if: A named operator, and one statement of what a new account gets that all of its pages agree on.

watchlist.name: Openference
watchlist.reason: The site's comparison copy still says "Free forever, no credit card", and OmniRoute's README lists it under "Free Forever — $0, no card", but the plans the site serves (api.openference.com/api/public/plans) start at Promo — priceMonthly 1 through Stripe, "2-day trial on all models, then Qwen3.8 & Llama 3.2", 420 requests a week — and then Lite at 15. No plan is priced at zero.
watchlist.reopen_if: The public plans API lists a plan priced at 0.

watchlist.name: Gemini Code Assist for individuals
watchlist.reason: The product page still sells "Gemini Code Assist for individuals at no cost" with last year's copy — "the power of Gemini 2.5 to your IDE at no cost (with Gemini 3 coming soon)" — but Google's developers blog of 2026-05-19 ended it: "On June 18, 2026, Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions will stop serving requests for Google AI Pro and Ultra, as well as those using it free of charge using Gemini Code Assist for individuals." The free individual plan moved to Antigravity, which is a row.
watchlist.reopen_if: Google's docs or blog say the Code Assist IDE extensions serve individual free users again.

watchlist.name: Cosine
watchlist.reason: Plans start at Starter, "$19 /month 4M credits/month", and the home page, read whole from a GitHub runner, never says "free".
watchlist.reopen_if: A free plan or no-card trial credit on cosine.sh/pricing.

watchlist.name: Refact.ai
watchlist.reason: Bring-your-own-key now. refact.ai/pricing is a 404, the main repository (smallcloudai/refact) was archived after 2026-05-30, and docs.refact.ai redirects to a fork's wiki whose setup page says "Refact is designed around BYOK rather than bundled cloud accounts".
watchlist.reopen_if: Refact bundles model usage again — a plan with included credits.

watchlist.name: Replit
watchlist.reason: "Start for free — no credit card required", but what the free Starter plan spends its AI on is Replit's own hosted workspace — the case CONTRIBUTING excludes, "hosted app builders whose free tokens are only spendable inside their own workspace".
watchlist.reopen_if: Free model access usable from a client or an endpoint outside Replit's workspace.

watchlist.name: Workshop AI (formerly Memex)
watchlist.reason: The $0 Discover plan carries "250 AI Credits", each "approximately $0.01 of model usage", spent inside "an AI creation platform to build websites, AI apps, dashboards, internal tools, and mobile apps" — an app builder, in the cloud or as its desktop app, not model access a developer can aim at code they already have.
watchlist.reopen_if: The credits become usable from other clients, or Workshop Desktop works as a coding agent on an existing project.

watchlist.name: ACLIDE
watchlist.reason: A gateway run by the French association Skyclouds whose Free plan gives "€20 Monthly usage credits", "Renewed every month · No credit card required". Its catalog serves most models twice: "distribué par l'endpoint Anthropic T2+ configuré par ACLIDE" at list price, and "est disponible via l'API unifiée ACLIDE" below it — and the second route carries all 36 zero-priced ids, Mistral's whole line, MiniMax M2.x, DeepSeek V4 and Qwen ':free' ids, other vendors' free quotas. Who runs that route is never named: the privacy page says only "Administration may select another secure AI endpoint operator". The xKiro case.
watchlist.reopen_if: The catalog names the operator behind "l'API unifiée ACLIDE", and it is the vendors' own capacity or sold to ACLIDE for this.

watchlist.name: Router9
watchlist.reason: A flat-rate "Token Plan" gateway with a Free plan, but no readable page states its quota or its models: "on the Free tier it draws only from free-eligible models", unnamed, and "Router9 fronts multiple providers and routes each request for the best value", also unnamed. The pricing page redirects to a login.
watchlist.reopen_if: The Free plan's quota and models on a public page, and the providers behind them named.

watchlist.name: Septor Labs
watchlist.reason: Unreadable: every page answers a bot challenge ("enable javascript and cookies to continue"), read directly and from a GitHub runner alike. The only statement of the offer is a router's label for it, "daily free-model quota".
watchlist.reopen_if: A page readable without a browser challenge that states the free quota.

watchlist.name: CLōD
watchlist.reason: "100 free daily requests, auto-replenished" across "50+ frontier and open-weight AI models", priced "always below the provider's list price cap" — a reseller that names neither the models the free requests reach nor where it buys them; its site renders client-side and docs.clod.io does not resolve.
watchlist.reopen_if: A readable page naming the free models and the supply behind them.

watchlist.name: BlazeAPI
watchlist.reason: Unreadable: blazeapi.org renders 30 characters without JavaScript and docs.blazeapi.org does not resolve. What is known of the offer is a router's label for it, "daily free tokens; Discord verification".
watchlist.reopen_if: Docs or a pricing page readable without JavaScript that state the free tokens.

watchlist.name: Lucidity Composite
watchlist.reason: A roleplay-first API whose free daily tier is other providers' capacity: "Composite runs a free daily tier of open-weight models, including Llama 3.3 70B, DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM 5.2, Kimi K2.6", and "For non LucidityAI models, OpenRouter is the upstream provider". The same page says both that "connecting a Discord account unlocks the free tier" and that "No Discord account, credit card, or invite is needed".
watchlist.reopen_if: The free tier runs on Lucidity's own infrastructure, with its models and quota stated once.

watchlist.name: DreamPrompting
watchlist.reason: Says what it is: "One free key routes across the free tiers of many providers with automatic failover" — "Free tiers first, trial credits next, keyless ch.at as the always-on last resort", over Groq, Mistral, NVIDIA NIM, Cohere, Google AI Studio, OpenRouter and Cloudflare. The offer is other vendors' free tiers under one key, the NaraRouter verdict.
watchlist.reopen_if: Free capacity of its own, or the vendors' consent to resell theirs.

watchlist.name: Waterfall
watchlist.reason: "The indie LLM router that tries free models first" — "waterfall routing from free to cheap to premium". A router serves nothing itself, so its 131 free models are other providers' free lanes re-served under its own key: the NaraRouter verdict.
watchlist.reopen_if: Free capacity of its own, named, with a quota.

watchlist.name: ElectronHub
watchlist.reason: One of the Discord-membership relays sources.yaml records under the YoannDev90 and zukixa lists, where nothing is a vendor's own offer; its site renders 639 characters without JavaScript, and a router's label for it is all that describes the free part, "shared weekly credits".
watchlist.reopen_if: A readable page that names the free credits and where they are served from.

watchlist.name: Alibaba Cloud Token Plan
watchlist.reason: "Token Plan is an AI model subscription service offered by Alibaba Cloud Model Studio", $6 to $68 a month; models.dev lists its rows at cost 0 because the usage is the subscription's. The free quota Model Studio does give is a row of its own.
watchlist.reopen_if: A Token Plan tier priced at zero.

watchlist.name: MiniMax Token Plan (China)
watchlist.reason: The Token Plan is a subscription — "Token Plan 通过订阅 Key 提供套餐内 Token Plan 用量额度" (the plan's quota, through a subscription key), bought as a personal subscription or credits — so its zero-cost rows on models.dev are included usage, not a free tier.
watchlist.reopen_if: A free quota on MiniMax's China platform that needs no subscription.

watchlist.name: EVREN (SSB)
watchlist.reason: The Turkish Presidency of Defence Industries' AI platform serves open models through an OpenAI-compatible API on H200s in Turkey, and its requests pass "kota ve kredi kontrollerinden" (through quota and credit checks), the credits earned by labelling data or spent on inference. The site has one way in, "e-Devlet ile Giriş Yap" (sign in with e-Devlet), through SSB's identity server on its EDEVLET realm — Turkey's state portal, which takes a Turkish identity number: a national identity wall. LLMTR's evren/* ids run on the caller's own EVREN key and are ignored on that row for the same reason.
watchlist.reopen_if: EVREN takes sign-ins that need no e-Devlet account.

watchlist.name: SambaNova Cloud (SambaCloud)
watchlist.reason: Listed from 2026-08-06 to 2026-09-23 as a free tier that applies while no payment method is linked, and taken off because a new account gets no free usage. The console's plans page, cloud.sambanova.ai/plans, read "Start exploring SambaNova Cloud with free API credits. No credit card required." in every Wayback capture up to 2026-06-20; by 2026-08-03 it read "Start exploring SambaNova Cloud. Add a payment method and purchase credits to run your first requests.", as it still does, and on 2026-08-12 a user on SambaNova's forum asked why, for a friend's new account, "a payment method is needed to use it" — unanswered. The docs' rate-limit page still describes a Free Tier "Applied when there is no payment method linked with your account", which is the page the row's probe read, so the probe passed through the change; the tier may hold for accounts that had free credits before it.
watchlist.reopen_if: The plans page offers free credits or free usage without a payment method again.

watchlist.name: Tencent Cloud TokenHub (international)
watchlist.reason: The international site's New User Free Trial Package gives each language model a million tokens valid a year, in a campaign to 2026-12-31, but "Each time you claim a free resource package for a model or enable postpaid service for a model, USD 1 will be automatically frozen in your account. If your account balance or credit limit is insufficient, the claim or enablement will fail" — a funded account, model by model (read 2026-09-26 in a browser). Its docs answer the project's client and the runners alike with EdgeOne's JavaScript challenge, so no probe could read a row back. The Chinese site, cloud.tencent.com, is a row (tencent-tokenhub) for accounts verified with mainland, Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan papers.
watchlist.reopen_if: The package can be claimed without a balance, or the offer is published on a page a probe can read.

watchlist.name: Fitten Code
watchlist.reason: A VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio and Vim coding assistant on Fitten's own model with no bring-your-own-key, whose individual use is free by its home page's pricing section and its FAQ — both rendered by script, which no probe can read: code.fittentech.com serves the project's client a 1 KB shell, and neither its VS Code nor its JetBrains marketplace description mentions a free plan (read 2026-09-27).
watchlist.reopen_if: A page the project's client can read — a static pricing or docs page, a marketplace description — states the free individual plan.

watchlist.name: CodeGeeX
watchlist.reason: Zhipu's IDE plugin says "CodeGeeX is available for free to all developers as a plugin product on your IDEs" in its VS Code and JetBrains marketplace descriptions, but its last VS Code release is 2025-09-01 and its last JetBrains one 2025-12-11, codegeex.cn serves a script shell, and nothing a probe reads would change the day the free service stopped answering — the descriptions are a year old (read 2026-09-27). Zhipu's current coding agent is the ZCode row.
watchlist.reopen_if: A release after 2025-12-11, or a page the client reads that states the free plugin plan today.

watchlist.name: Codebuff
watchlist.reason: Paid only: subscriptions or "Pay just 1¢ per credit" on codebuff.com/pricing (read 2026-09-27). The same company's free product is Freebuff, a row.
watchlist.reopen_if: codebuff.com publishes a free allowance of its own.

watchlist.name: Pieces for Developers
watchlist.reason: "Is Pieces free to use? No. … New users start with a 7-day free trial on any plan", and "Starting the 7-day Pro trial takes a card on file" (pieces.app/pricing, read 2026-09-27) — a trial behind a card, which CONTRIBUTING excludes.
watchlist.reopen_if: A plan or trial without a card on file.

watchlist.name: GoCodeo
watchlist.reason: Its pricing page still offers a Hobby plan that "Includes 50 premium model requests per month 1000 autocompletions 100 basic model requests" and calls the VS Code agent "free forever with limited requests", but the extension's last release is 2025-07-09, fourteen months before this read, and a page that stands still is no sign the service answers — the probe would vouch for a product that may be gone (read 2026-09-27).
watchlist.reopen_if: A release after 2025-07-09, or other evidence that the agent still serves its free requests.

watchlist.name: goose (Block, now Agentic AI Foundation)
watchlist.reason: An open-source agent that brings no model of its own: "Works with 15+ providers … Use API keys or your existing Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions via ACP" (goose-docs.ai), and its free options are other vendors' free tiers — "not all supported LLM Providers provide a free tier" (goose-docs.ai/docs/getting-started/providers/, read 2026-09-27). BYOK only.
watchlist.reopen_if: goose ships a hosted model lane of its own with a free allowance.

watchlist.name: Pi coding agent
watchlist.reason: "15+ providers, hundreds of models … Authenticate via API keys or OAuth" (pi.dev, read 2026-09-27): bring your own key or subscription, no bundled model usage.
watchlist.reopen_if: Pi bundles a free model allowance of its own.

watchlist.name: Sourcegraph Cody
watchlist.reason: "As of July 23, 2025, the following plans will no longer be available: Cody Free, Cody Pro" (Sourcegraph's blog, read 2026-09-27); Cody is an Enterprise product now. Lists still carry the free tier.
watchlist.reopen_if: Sourcegraph offers an individual plan with free Cody usage again.

watchlist.name: Onomeo
watchlist.reason: A one-person gateway over other vendors' free tiers: "The free-route models run on the free tier each provider offers; onomeo puts them behind one key", and "Big models such as Claude and GPT are paid for by onomeo, within a shared daily budget" (onomeo.com/models, read 2026-09-27). The free tiers it routes to are rows here in their own right; a gateway's free plan over them is a watchlist verdict, never a row.
watchlist.reopen_if: Onomeo serves models of its own, or buys the capacity it gives away, and says so.

watchlist.name: YingSuan AI
watchlist.reason: A reseller of other vendors' models whose free offer is a one-off trial: "Start free with 100 requests — no credit card, no payment required" (yingsuan.top/payment.html, read 2026-09-27) — a hundred calls, then paid.
watchlist.reopen_if: A recurring free allowance, or free models it serves itself.

watchlist.name: Kira AI
watchlist.reason: A Vietnamese gateway whose own "Kira" models, by its FAQ, combine in-house open-source models with "OpenAI (GPT 5.5), Claude (Claude 4.8) và Gemini (Gemini 3 trở lên)", its packages apply "chỉ áp dụng cho model Kira" (only to the kira- models), and partner models are paid from a VND wallet (kiraai.vn/faq/, read 2026-09-27). No chat model is free in its own right.
watchlist.reopen_if: A kira- chat model is priced at zero, with the models behind it named.

watchlist.name: Atlas Cloud
watchlist.reason: Its get-started guide asks for money first — "The minimum top-up amount is $25" (atlascloud.ai/docs/en/get-started, read 2026-09-27) — while its model pages say "New users receive free credits to explore the platform and test models", of no stated size and with no stated way to reach them before paying: the SiliconFlow record.
watchlist.reopen_if: A page states the free credit's size and that it is spent before any payment step.

watchlist.name: Databricks Free Edition
watchlist.reason: Free and non-commercial ("Free Edition accounts may not be used for commercial purposes"), in a "serverless-only, quota-limited environment" where you can "experiment with foundation models", but its limits page names no model and no quota for them — "Certain models not available" — and the endpoint is each workspace's own (docs.databricks.com/aws/en/getting-started/free-edition and free-edition-limitations, read 2026-09-27). A reader cannot tell what they would be calling.
watchlist.reopen_if: Databricks documents which foundation models a Free Edition workspace can query and at what limits.

watchlist.name: ZeroTwo
watchlist.reason: An AI workspace over other vendors' models whose Free plan is chat — "15 messages per day" with a "Limited model selection", "no card required" (zerotwo.ai/pricing, read 2026-09-29). Its coding agent, ZeroCode, a desktop agent for local repositories, is "Not included" on Free in the plan table, which gives it from Plus at $14.99 a month (the docs, from Pro); the code-agent page's "Free to try" meets that table, and the table is the specific statement. Chat messages in a workspace are not model use a coding agent or an endpoint can spend.
watchlist.reopen_if: ZeroCode comes with the Free plan, or a free allowance a coding agent or an endpoint can spend.

watchlist.name: AssemblyAI (LLM Gateway)
watchlist.reason: Its no-card free tier is speech. The pricing page answers "Can I sign up for free?" with "You can create an account and start transcribing immediately with no credit card required. The free tier includes up to 185 hours of pre-recorded transcription and up to 333 hours of streaming transcription." Its LLM Gateway is OpenAI-compatible, at https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1, "One API for Claude, GPT, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi, and more", but the gateway's rate-limit page gives the Free account type "Not available" and a Paid one 30 requests a minute per model (assemblyai.com/pricing, docs/llm-gateway/rate-limits, read 2026-09-30). pacocartones/free-llm-api-hub lists the signup credit beside the gateway as though the one reached the other.
watchlist.reopen_if: The LLM Gateway's rate-limit page gives free accounts a limit, or an AssemblyAI page says the free tier reaches the gateway.

watchlist.name: Contextual AI
watchlist.reason: A RAG platform: its pricing page offers "Claim your $25 in free credits" on the on-demand plan, spent on datastores, agents and component APIs for parsing, reranking and grounded generation. Text comes out of its agents and out of Generate, a POST to https://api.contextual.ai/v1/generate for its Grounded Language Model, "an LLM engineered specifically to prioritize faithfulness to in-context retrievals", capped at 32,000 tokens a request; nothing in its documentation index (docs.contextual.ai/llms.txt, read 2026-09-30) is a chat-completions or messages endpoint a coding agent could be pointed at, so the credit buys nothing this list carries.
watchlist.reopen_if: Contextual AI documents an OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible chat endpoint that the free credit reaches.

watchlist.name: TokenToWorld
watchlist.reason: Known only from three repositories an account opened on 2026-06-03 — willianhecaiyan/claude-no-creditcard-demo, TOKENTOWORLD and fix-openai-429-demo — which sell it as Claude 3, GPT-4o, DeepSeek, Kimi and Qwen for developers "lacking US credit card", with a "Stable multi-source balance to avoid interface blocking", wholesale and affiliate terms, and "trial tokens" of no stated size. Nothing answers to read: tokentoworld.com and www refuse HTTPS here and from a GitHub runner on 2026-09-30, and plain HTTP returns nginx's 404 page. A relay whose offer cannot be read cannot be verified to offer anything, the rule that settled Clarifai, Coze and Morph, and the ad does not say where the Claude it sells comes from.
watchlist.reopen_if: tokentoworld.com serves its terms over HTTPS, stating a trial spent before any payment and where its Claude supply comes from.

watchlist.name: Lightning AI (Model APIs)
watchlist.reason: Its Model APIs are OpenAI-compatible, take Claude Code through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, and "Users get up to 40 million free tokens to start" at 15 requests a minute on the Free plan (docs/platform/inference/model-apis). The account is free — "no credit card required" to create it, a non-virtual phone number to verify it — and "Eligible free plan users receive complimentary credits", which "can be used for compute, inference, and storage" and are "promotional" (the getting-started, FAQ and billing pages, read 2026-09-30). No page says the credits reach an account without a card, and the console offers them beside a card: its billing panel pairs "Claim your … free credits" with an "Add card" button, and its sign-up promises "up to 30 free credits". The 44 models of the keyless catalog at lightning.ai/api/v1/models are all priced, Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra among them, so the credit is the whole offer — the SiliconFlow record, the card question open.
watchlist.reopen_if: A Lightning page says the free credits reach an account without a card, or a model in its catalog is priced at zero.

watchlist.name: QwenCloud
watchlist.reason: Alibaba's developer platform for Qwen and third-party models, run by Intelligent Cloud Computing (Singapore), OpenAI-compatible at https://maas.qwencloudapi.com/compatible-mode/v1 with Claude Code and Codex guides. Its homepage says "Most models offer free API credits", and its free-quota page gives each model a quota valid 90 days from activation, but the way in is "Sign up for QwenCloud and complete your payment information to activate your free quota" (docs.qwencloud.com/resources/free-quota, read 2026-09-30) — a credit behind payment details, which CONTRIBUTING does not take. Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's international free quota is a row.
watchlist.reopen_if: A QwenCloud page grants the free quota before any payment information is given.
